items.article: The dark side of the prediction market boom is becoming more clear: Experts say the sites have become go-to outlets for gambling addicts to relapse as the companies avoid state consumer protections. During the pandemic, Thomas thought he would give DraftKings and FanDuel a try. Before long, he formed a habit. "I could have ten drinks one night and then be fine with not drinking again for a year," said Thomas, 35, who asked to be identified by his middle name fearing his problem gambling history could affect his career. "But sports gambling was different. It really got me." He never cared much for sports. Yet betting on games seemed like an easy way to make a buck. He started placing wagers on football and tennis mostly using parlays, which are difficult-to-win bets that require multiple things happening in one game in order to land an enticing payout. Working from his home in Pennsylvania in the financial services industry, Thomas says there were few moments when he didn't have one eye on placing a bet as he juggled work emails and meetings. When his paycheck arrived, he'd quickly squander it all trying to dig himself out of a gambling hole, only to find himself even deeper in. This cycle continued for years, with Thomas racking up around $75,000 in debt from credit cards and personal loans. He ended up more than $50,000 in the red from online sportsbooks.

items.article: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived an execution attempt Wednesday night after being administered two doses of pentobarbital and transported to a hospital, raising an unusual legal question: Can a state try to execute someone a second time after a failed execution? The answer appears to be yes, though Pike's case could present complications depending on her medical condition and what investigators ultimately determine went wrong during the execution attempt. The central legal question is whether a second execution attempt would violate the Eighth Amendment's prohibition on cruel and unusual punishment. Eric Berger, the Earl Dunlap Distinguished Professor of Law at the University of Nebraska who has written extensively on lethal injection litigation, told Newsweek that the strongest precedent favors Tennessee's ability to seek another execution date. "Probably," Berger said when asked whether Tennessee can legally attempt to execute Pike again. "The Supreme Court in Louisiana ex rel. Francis v. Resweber found that the Eighth Amendment does not categorically bar a state from attempting a second execution after the first execution attempt fails." The failed execution has already prompted Governor Bill Lee to order a third-party review and pause Tennessee's remaining scheduled executions for 2026. Diesel prices in the UK have reached a record high, according to the RAC, hitting £2 a litre for the first time as the war in the Middle East continues to drive up the cost of oil worldwide. The price of a litre in the UK has risen 40.5 per cent since late February, when the US first launched strikes against Iran, while prices are also at a record high in the US, where much of the world’s supply is produced and refined. In response to rising costs, Donald Trump has indicated he will ask European countries to draw from their diesel reserves as he threatens a ban on US exports of the fuel. Since 2022, the US has become the world’s largest exporter of diesel by a wide margin as the Ukraine conflict has reduced demand for Russian fuel, alongside its ability to refine it. Around 30 per cent of all cars on the road in the UK are fuelled by diesel, rising to 38 per cent of HGVs. Higher costs to operate these vehicles could have an impact on the cost of goods.

items.article: By planting gardens and restoring ecosystems around its data centers, Microsoft thinks it can be a “better neighbor.” But is it enough? Microsoft is expanding ‘biomimicry’ at its data centers as it faces more pushback from locals over construction, pollution, and noise. San Antonio City Councilmember Ric Galvan remembers when data centers first arrived in his city in the 2000s, looking like relatively unassuming office buildings. But that’s changed in recent years, as data centers have grown into massive “hyperscale” facilities spanning millions of square feet and housing the physical infrastructure for AI. There are now more than a dozen data centers in Galvan’s roughly 55-square-mile district, and he expects that number to grow to around 20 over the next few years if proposed projects are completed. They’re clustered along two main roads, concentrating nuisances in the same neighborhoods: traffic and trees cut down during construction, followed by constant bright lights and noise when the data center is operating. A lot of the area used to be green fields, he explains, allowing many residents to feel close to nature. items.text: Christa Pike survived attempted execution. What now?
items.article: The nation is awaiting answers after the botched execution of murderer Christa Pike on Sept. 30 resulted in her hospitalization in critical condition. Pike, 50, survived two rounds of lethal injection drugs and was taken by ambulance to a hospital, her attorneys have said. “We don’t have much sense of her prognosis but we do know that she is alive right now and receiving lifesaving medical care,” Randy Spivey, one of Pike’s attorneys, said on Oct. 1. Attorneys said her condition was unchanged as of late the night of Oct. 1. USA TODAY has reached out to Pike's legal team on Oct. 2 for any updates to her status. Tennessee officials have meanwhile said little about Pike's health condition or how the lethal injection could have failed. The Department of Correction said it followed protocol. The failed execution prompted Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to call for an independent investigation and put a pause on executions in the state for the remainder of the year. He called what happened in Pike's death chamber "disturbing" and a "tragedy." "How does that happen?" he said on Oct. 1. "It shouldn’t be very difficult." Pike was to be put to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend brutally tortured and killed Slemmer. The execution attempt came after a chaotic day of last-minute legal wrangling that went all the way up to the U.S. Supreme Court.

items.article: Abhijeet Dipke explains why the Cockroach Janta Party chose Mumbai instead of Delhi for its ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Abhijeet Dipke led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has started its planned 'Jail Bharo Andolan' against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai on Friday, 2 October. The protest is being held at Shivaji Park in Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti despite Mumbai Police denied the permission. AI-generated summary, reviewed by editors The CJP had announced that protest would begin at 4 PM near Gate no. 6 of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park. Now CJP founder Dipke said Mumbai was chosen because of he major difference between election results of 2024 Lok Sabha Elections and Maharashtra Assembly election held within six months gap. CJP has raised question about electoral rolls and how the Election Commission function. The protest started after an Indian Express report found differences within the poll panel over decisions related to Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls. However, the Election Commission has made it clear that the decisions were taken through the prescribed institutional process. Dipke has defended the decision to hold the agitation on 2 October, referring to Mahatma Gandhi's role in India's freedom movement. "We are fighting against those in power...We all remember Mahatma Gandhi, who fought against the Britishers. Did the British ever permit him to agitate?" he said.

items.text: How Gordon became one of England's main men
items.article: Anthony Gordon has been England's in-form player since the World Cup knockout stage - is the Barcelona forward now undroppable? Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Declan Rice, Jordan Pickford and now Anthony Gordon. All have become guaranteed starters and reliable stars for England, with the Barcelona winger the latest to look, according to captain Kane, like one of the Three Lions' "main men". Gordon was one of England's standout players at the World Cup and earned a big-money move to European giants Barca in the summer, while his good form has continued into his country's Nations League campaign. He scored the opening goal in England's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night, after also netting in a 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday. In fact, the 25-year-old's England form has been building since the knockout stage of the World Cup began - his run of averaging a goal contribution every 69 minutes started with assisting both Kane's efforts in a 2-1 last-32 victory over DR Congo. The former Newcastle player has scored three goals and provided three assists in his past six England matches, while he also won the penalty in England's dramatic last-16 victory over Mexico at Azteca Stadium.

Here's how banks stocks have performed in past on leadership change announcements Shares of HDFC Bank , will remain in focus on Monday, October 5, after India’s largest private lender announced the appointment of Anup Bagchi as its next chief of executive for a period of three years. Fifty five year old Anup Bagchi will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, who decided to not seek reappointment after his second tenure ends in October 2026. Sashidhar Jagdishan’s departure has come just months after Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March, saying certain practices at the bank were at odds with his “personal values and ethics”.
